data.source_title: Improving Emergency Department radiology transportation time: a successful implementation of lean methodology
data.locator: Methods, Theoretical model and outcome measure (pp. 2-3); Results, Table 2 (p. 6); Discussion (p. 6).
data.source_setting: Emergency department, American University of Beirut Medical Center; plain radiography patients.
data.source_period: Pre-intervention 2012-10-17 to 2013-04-17; post-intervention 2013-05-19 to 2013-11-19, after one-month washout.
data.source_n: 6,186 pre-intervention radiographs; 4,879 post-intervention radiographs. Excludes 00:00-08:00 radiographs and patients leaving against medical advice or transferred.
data.quantity: Cashier order-processing to radiographer study-initiation transportation turnaround time
data.source_evidence_basis: Inspected publisher full text and university repository PDF. Methods explicitly define transportation TAT as cashier processing to PACS-recorded radiographer study initiation. Discussion later calls this the order-processing-to-study-completion step, while Methods distinguish initiation-to-completion as a separate interval.
data.limitations: Single center, retrospective nonrandomized pre/post operational study; exclusions and concurrent ED changes constrain transfer. The discussion endpoint wording conflicts with the operational definition in Methods.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Use as external reference for cashier-processed order to imaging-study initiation elapsed time, following the explicit Methods definition; do not relabel it as image completion or reporting time, and do not transfer as RWJ measurement.
data.conflict_resolution: interpretable_convention: Methods endpoint retained; conflicting Discussion shorthand preserved as limitation
